description: No February 2021 public protest gathering in Qatar is confirmed. Nine captured batched search actions and two opened out-of-month reports improve boundary review but do not establish that no February protest occurred.
required_followup: Retain the unknown-coverage assessment. If future discovery produces a dated February event lead, test occurrence, month ownership, public-gathering threshold and own-state demand under the source protocol; do not create an absence record.

description: The two opened security-guard wage reports are outside February: S001 says “Wednesday” in the week before 10 May (calendar context implies 5 May, not printed), and S002 conflicts between 26 March and 26 April. The other seven cards remain search-only and do not establish event dates.
required_followup: Only pursue exact dates for the seven unread leads if a captured header warrants it. Check January–March boundaries and distinguish publication date, event start and any later report before assigning a unit.

description: S001 reports hundreds of guards and protests at various sites but supplies no location-specific simultaneous count; it does not support assigning the full qualitative total to one gathering. S002 says a group protested but gives no estimate. The seven search-only cards do not verify attendance.
required_followup: For any future February event lead, establish turnout at the same physical public gathering. Do not equate workforce totals, several sites, vehicles or planned participation with simultaneous attendance of at least 50.

description: S001 describes employer salary/overtime violations and days-off grievances; S002 describes a salary increase/minimum-wage demand directed to company management. Neither opened report establishes a distinct original demand addressed to Qatar’s government or policy. A government response is not itself proof of a state target.
required_followup: Keep own-state demand unresolved for these reports and inspect exact demands/action form in any future eligible February lead. Do not equate a private wage claim, state enforcement response, work refusal or announced action with an eligible state-directed public gathering.

description: S001 and S002 identify different employers and different out-of-month date periods. S003–S005 and S008 are Business and Human Rights Resource Centre headers that may reuse related wage reporting; the pages remain unread, so same-story/origin and independent corroboration are unresolved.
required_followup: If a future dated February lead merits follow-up, compare employer, date, location, attribution and explicit written-origin links after a fresh source-specific gate. Do not count repeated/syndicated headers as independent confirmation.

description: The discovery pass searched English and Arabic. It did not systematically search migrant-community languages or establish completeness of Qatar local-language indexing.
required_followup: If a concrete February event lead emerges, prioritize relevant local outlets and migrant-community languages where search sources are available, then report remaining language and archive limitations.

description: Two current-unit body reads (S001 and S002) are recorded with exact-URL receipts, contemporaneous manual reviews, request outcomes and scoped notes. Seven cards (S003–S009) remain search_only. S002’s earlier January consultation is not transferred to this unit’s read count.
required_followup: Do not request more bodies without a new explicit read phase and a fresh stable exact-URL receipt, complete manual publisher/origin review, byte-identical readback and full live-input comparison. Reuse source-specific access evidence only under the existing protocol.

description: Open-web searches do not reproduce the original LexisNexis newspaper workflow. The latest official baseline, universe, schema and separate Coding Procedure remain unverified.
required_followup: Retain the fixed cutoff and pending official-baseline gate; coordinator review must reconcile search-method differences and verify the baseline before official use.
